title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre on 1982-10-09
lineage: Cassette (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby C) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/48k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.1 -> FLAC/16
source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90/Dolby B) -> Cassette (JVC KD-V6/XLII-S90/Dolby C)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of an electrifying 1982 show featuring a smoking Touch of Grey/West L.A., tight Eyes, soaring Morning Dew and a monster Other One.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the best of ’82, with an energetic first set highlighted by Touch of Grey and West L.A. Fadeaway, and a second set that flows flawlessly through Eyes, Estimated Prophet, The Other One, Morning Dew and a rousing encore. The soundboard (SBD) source is described as crisp, upgraded and perfectly balanced, giving listeners crystal‑clear guitar tones, deep drums with great stereo separation, and overall superb audio fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: All three reviews award five stars, praising both the musical performance (standout songs, high energy) and the flawless soundboard recording; consistent enthusiastic feedback yields a near‑perfect rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with upgraded SBD source; excellent stereo separation, deep drums, pure guitar tone, no reported dropouts or muffiness. A good matrix version also exists.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong momentum and transitions smoothly into a second set that is tightly paced, with seamless segues between songs and an especially cohesive climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone described as purest ever; channels Dylan on Touch of Grey, delivers soaring solos and rotor‑pan work during The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass intuition highlighted during the spacey improvisations; provides powerful support in the dark, dissonant sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals strained but power through; rhythm guitar contributions noted throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work praised for its role in the psychedelic jams and tight interplay with guitars.
band_member_comments.Drums: Deep, resonant drum sound with excellent stereo separation; drums take the reins during key improvisational passages.
